sections.note: Begins with two lines of prose (326-328). Each entry is '_Station._--Keeper name(s).--' followed by notes and quotes. Most give keepers' names, so they matter for the roll. One station's entry can run over several paragraphs that do not repeat the station name (N. Unst 330-371; Pentland Skerries 386-417). Bracketed editorial notes end '--J. A. H.-B.]'. sections.title: Separate Report under Genera and Species.
head_examples: _February._--A single record of Blackbird at Pentland Skerries on 24th.
sections.note: Ordered by family, not species. Each family opens mid-line ('Family.--' and then the first month in the same paragraph). The months follow as their own paragraphs ('_Month._--') and never repeat the family name, so a cutter has to carry the family forward. Month order is sometimes broken (Fringillidæ goes back to _August_ after _December_, 638-643), and some months are written without italics ('Hirundinidæ.--May.--'). There are runs of pure prose with no records: Pelecanidæ on Gannets (775-789), the Ardeidæ introduction (791-801, then '_Report._--_March._--'), and the Charadriidæ and Scolopacidæ remarks. Procellariidæ appears twice (857, 932). Lines 966-969 are blank.

Each entry is 'Month Nth.--' followed by several stations in one paragraph, one after another: '_Name_ L.H.,' / '_Name_ L.V.,', each followed by its wind and weather in parentheses. The station has to be split out mid-line. Not every place is a light: Redcar, Yarmouth, Thanet, Great Cotes, Tetney, Seaton-Carew, Cley and Blakeney, Northrepps and Spurn appear as well. Some are not italicised ('Thanet,' 1257; 'Yarmouth,' 1358; 'Redcar,' 2553). At 1042 '[1]' sits before '_Flambro'_L.H.' with no space. '_S. S. Head_ L.V.' is South Sand Head. Footnotes sit between entries at 1045-1048, 1364-1366 and 1943-1945. 1235 has 'March 26th--' with no period. Lines 1339 and 2602 begin with a month name but continue the entry before them: split only on 'Month Nth.--'. Bracketed asides like 1338 '[A pair nested ...]' fall inside entries. There is no break between spring and autumn.

Columns are species, how received, how procured, date as 'DD/ M mo.' and station. Ditto marks fill the species and method columns. sections.title: List of Birds Noticed.
sections.note: Two-column index of the Irish species, with printed page numbers, in two blocks (5444, and '--continued.' at 5485). It is the contents of the species section that follows, not observations.

Each species heading is a line of its own, with blank lines around it: an English name, usually followed by '(_Latin_, Authority).', or a quoted name ('"Stonechat."', '"Tits."', '"Geese."'). Two headings span two lines (7459-7460 Common Snipe and Jack Snipe; 7904-7905 Cormorant and Shag). 7004 has its Latin name without underscores. Under each heading there is one paragraph per station, '_Station._--Month Nth, ...', running round the coast from Fastnet. A cutter can split into species × station. Exceptions: 6302 'Tory Island.--' has no underscores, and 7534 ("Greenshank.") has no station at all. Station names include light-ship forms ('_Coningbeg Light-ship._', '_Arklow South Light-ship._') and '_South Maidens._'/'_North Maidens._'. Some entries carry dates from January 1888. Editorial brackets ('[Leg and wing received.]', '--R. M. B.]') fall mid-entry and can begin a line (5764, 6553), and some entries just point elsewhere ('(See under Starling.)'). Ends with 'Birds not Identified.' (8151-8159) and a row of asterisks at 8162 that is not part of it.

notes:
The file has CRLF line endings, so a regex anchored with '$' needs '\r?$'. Line numbers are the Read tool's. The 33 sections cover lines 1-8524 with no gaps or overlaps.

Where the observations are, by coast:
- East and West Scotland have no diary. Their records are in the station extracts and the species reports, which are ordered by family. In both reports the family name opens mid-line ('Turdidæ.--', 'Saxicolinæ.--_January._--') and is not repeated on the '_Month._--' paragraphs that follow, so a cutter has to carry it forward.
- The two English coasts have diaries: 'Month Nth.--' entries in which several stations run on in one paragraph, each followed by its weather in parentheses.
- Ireland is ordered by species, with one '_Station._--' paragraph per station under each species heading.

Sections marked 'summary' repeat records that are given in full elsewhere: the general remarks, and the wing and leg tables, which also confirm identifications. Station lists are marked station_list with observations none.

Things I left as printed rather than splitting further:
- The diaries are marked season 'both', because the report never divides them into spring and autumn; only month headings mark the time.
- The West England diary has no July.
- The East Scotland species report contains prose with no records (Gannets 775-789; Herons 791-801), and so does the West Scotland 'Remarks.' at 3002-3012.

Keeper names, which matter for the roll, are in five places:
- the East England list, 984-1019;
- the West England list, 3349-3427, plus surnames in the thanks at 3428-3437;
- the Irish list, 5187-5248, plus names in the Irish preface (e.g. 5019-5020, 5037-5042);
- the station entries for East Scotland (324-443) and West Scotland (2849-3001), which are not in a list at all.
